name: Hartford
why: Casual shirts and clothing in an American 1960s style, made from Italian and Japanese cloth by a Paris company.
origin: Founded in 1979 by Yves Chareton; his children Marina and Yann now run parts of the business.

onething.n: the founding object — deadstock chambray started the brand; verify link

notes.fren: a Frenchman selling America back to both continents — the Palm Angels pattern, a generation early
notes.cotton: founded on deadstock oxford and chambray — Albini and Maruwa on the labels
notes.craft: Hartford's about page names Albini, Maruwa and Liberty as cloth sources, and every product page states where the cloth was woven, dyed and sewn, mostly Morocco, with a short unnamed profile of the contract workshop (e.g. a family shirt factory near Casablanca making Hartford shirts for 30+ years). It owns no making, and on the product pages it names neither mill nor factory. A weak 3: unusually transparent, but the names sit on the about page.

craft_evidence.owned_d: No owned factory. PDPs describe contract makers ('notre façonnier', 'notre atelier partenaire'), unnamed: a family shirt factory near Casablanca (~300 people, 30+ years with Hartford, ICS-audited); a trouser maker in the Fès region (20+ years); a multi-product 'façon' workshop in Marrakech (~200 people); a jersey/knit workshop near Braga, Portugal (founded 1995, ~40 people). About page: studio in Paris, design only.
craft_evidence.countries: Morocco 6/9, Portugal 1/9, China 1/9, India 1/9 (sample of 9 men's PDPs: 5 shirts, corduroy trouser, wool flannel jacket, merino knit, slub tee, suede jacket). PDPs also give weaving/knitting, dyeing and sewing countries separately.
